subject: Reusable research principles distilled from B1 V3 Phase 9-14B

lessons.title: Single-variable ablation can be severely misleading
lessons.principle: Removing one filter at a time will under-state the importance of conditionally-active filters by an order of magnitude.

evidence.phase12a_finding: B_KltD single-removal Jaccard 1.000 in all 3 windows; ΔPF 0.000
evidence.phase14b_finding: B_KltD paired with A_J_range gives int_PF -0.944 below additive

lessons.rule: Treat single-ablation 'redundancy' as a hypothesis. Confirm with at least one remove-pair test.

lessons.title: Interaction effects must be tested before declaring redundancy
lessons.principle: Default-config redundancy can mask conditional bridges.

evidence.phase14b_revealed: Prefilter_KltD (B_KltD) is a conditional bridge, not redundant

lessons.title: Return retention is insufficient for declaring alpha preservation
lessons.principle: A reduced system that matches total return can still be a different strategy with worse risk-adjusted performance.
lessons.rule: Always report PF, Sharpe, max drawdown, AND trade-level Jaccard. Return alone is a 1-D shadow.

lessons.title: Jaccard (trade-level overlap) should always be tracked
lessons.principle: Two backtests with similar headline metrics can be entirely different strategies.

evidence.phase12b: alpha-only Jaccard 0.034-0.051 despite similar return magnitudes

lessons.title: PF retention is more important than return retention
lessons.principle: Profit factor proxies the quality of the win/loss distribution. Return proxies magnitude. A system can match return by simultaneously trading more winners and more losers, but PF will drop.
lessons.rule: For any 'alpha preservation' claim require PF retention >= 80% AND Sharpe retention >= 80% AND Jaccard >= 0.50 in all windows.

lessons.title: Independent alpha != sufficient alpha
lessons.principle: A system can have N independent alpha sources and still fail to function without additional concentrators.
lessons.rule: Independence is necessary but not sufficient. Always test the minimum reconstruction (keep only independent alpha, remove rest).

lessons.title: Generator-driven and constraint-geometry systems require different audits
lessons.principle: A generator-driven system can be decomposed into independent factors; a constraint-geometry system cannot.
lessons.diagnostic: Run 'remove everything except verified alpha'. If trade identity or PF collapses, switch to interaction-based audit.

lessons.title: Sensitivity != robustness != independence
lessons.principle: Each audit class produces a different kind of claim. Do not conflate them.
lessons.rule: Only parameters surviving all three of (sensitivity, robustness, independence) are confirmed independent alpha.

lessons.title: Dead in default config != dead in all configs
lessons.principle: A filter with Jaccard 1.000 under defaults may activate under different configurations.
lessons.rule: Mark 'dead under <config>'. Do not delete parameters that look dead under one configuration.

lessons.title: Universe choice shapes the visible alpha
lessons.principle: Conclusions about 'no other alpha exists' hold only for the feature universe currently exposed at runtime.
lessons.rule: Before declaring 'no other alpha exists', audit coverage. The honest conclusion is 'no other alpha is visible in the current universe'.

lessons.title: Higher-order interactions exist and can dominate pairs
lessons.principle: Some constraint systems have effective dimension >= 3; three-way removal effects can exceed any two-way effect.
lessons.rule: When pair interactions are strong, test triples for the strongest pairs.

lessons.title: Anti-alpha components exist; do not confuse with regime artefacts
lessons.principle: A filter whose removal improves performance is anti-alpha at current settings. But anti-alpha-by-single-removal can also be a hub constraint whose true role is interactive.
lessons.rule: Single-removal positive ΔPF is a red flag but not a verdict. Check pair interactions before reclassifying as anti-alpha.

lessons.title: Constraint hubs have a recognisable fingerprint
lessons.principle: High positive single ΔPF (looks anti-alpha) + dominant negative pair interactions with several other constraints = structural hub.
lessons.rule: Never delete a constraint with the hub fingerprint based on single-removal evidence alone.

lessons.title: Document with evidence, not confidence
lessons.principle: Every claim in closure reports should cite the phase / file / metric.
lessons.rule: Refuse to accept claims without citations. Make closure documents auditable.

lessons.title: Treat B1 V3 as a completed research subject
lessons.principle: Further optimization on B1 V3 should not begin from feature search or threshold tuning. Real progress requires extending the feature universe (Phase 14A ranked missing categories).
lessons.rule: Future agents touching B1 V3 must read ag2_research/knowledge_base/b1_v3/verdict_full.md and architecture_full.md first. They must not propose changes to existing concentrators or generators without re-running Phase 12B / Phase 14B-equivalent interaction tests.

summary.key_meta_lesson: A system can look generator-driven on the surface and be constraint-geometric in reality. Always check by minimum-reconstruction before committing to a decomposition.
